_comment: Verified public-domain nursery rhymes. A rhyme may be used ONLY if it appears here with pd_verified=true. Adding a row is a compliance decision: verify the source, then log it in audit/decision_log.csv. Every entry here is a COMPOSITION cleared for use; the RECORDING must always be our own original work-for-hire (see compliance/music-licensing-basics.md).
verification_standard: First publication in print before 1930 (95-year term under 17 U.S.C. 304 has expired), verified against a citable printed source.

rhymes.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star
rhymes.pd_basis: Lyrics from Jane Taylor, 'The Star', Rhymes for the Nursery (1806). Melody from 'Ah! vous dirai-je, maman' (published 1761).
rhymes.source: Taylor, Ann and Jane. Rhymes for the Nursery. London: Darton and Harvey, 1806.
rhymes.learning_hook: stars, day and night, gentle wind-down
rhymes.notes: Melody is shared with the Alphabet Song and Baa Baa Black Sheep. Vary the arrangement so our three uses do not sound like the same track.

rhymes.title: The Itsy Bitsy Spider
rhymes.first_line: The itsy bitsy spider climbed up the waterspout
rhymes.pd_basis: Traditional; printed in collections well before 1930, including as 'spider song' in Camp and Camp Fire Activities (1910s) and earlier variants.
rhymes.source: Traditional American children's song; pre-1930 printed collections.
rhymes.learning_hook: weather cycle, hand actions, cause and effect, trying again
rhymes.notes: Strong finger-play song. Good for action-modelling without any call to action.

rhymes.title: Old MacDonald Had a Farm
rhymes.pd_basis: Traditional; printed as 'Ohio' in Tommy's Tunes (1917) and in Traditional Ballads and Folk Songs (1922).
rhymes.source: Tommy's Tunes, ed. F. T. Nettleingham, 1917.
rhymes.learning_hook: animal names and sounds, repetition, cumulative memory
rhymes.notes: Cumulative structure gives natural variation between videos: change which animals and their order.

rhymes.title: Row, Row, Row Your Boat
rhymes.first_line: Row, row, row your boat, gently down the stream
rhymes.pd_basis: Printed in The Franklin Square Song Collection (1881).
rhymes.source: The Franklin Square Song Collection, New York: Harper and Brothers, 1881.
rhymes.learning_hook: rowing motion, rhythm and steady beat, round singing
rhymes.notes: Very short. Needs a scene arc rather than verse count to fill runtime.

rhymes.title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
rhymes.first_line: Mary had a little lamb, its fleece was white as snow
rhymes.pd_basis: Sarah Josepha Hale, Poems for Our Children (1830); melody by Lowell Mason (1830s).
rhymes.source: Hale, Sarah Josepha. Poems for Our Children. Boston: Marsh, Capen and Lyon, 1830.
rhymes.notes: Narrative rhyme - suits a story arc across scenes.

rhymes.title: Hickory Dickory Dock
rhymes.first_line: Hickory dickory dock, the mouse ran up the clock
rhymes.pd_basis: Printed in Tommy Thumb's Pretty Song Book (c. 1744).
rhymes.source: Tommy Thumb's Pretty Song Book, London, c. 1744.
rhymes.learning_hook: telling the hour, counting to twelve, up and down
rhymes.notes: Natural counting extension: one o'clock, two o'clock. Good numeracy hook.

rhymes.title: London Bridge Is Falling Down
rhymes.pd_basis: Traditional; printed in Tommy Thumb's Pretty Song Book (c. 1744) and Gammer Gurton's Garland (1784).
rhymes.learning_hook: materials and building, repairing what is broken
rhymes.notes: Keep the visuals constructive - building and mending, never collapse or peril.

rhymes.title: Baa, Baa, Black Sheep
rhymes.first_line: Baa, baa, black sheep, have you any wool?
rhymes.pd_basis: Printed in Tommy Thumb's Pretty Song Book (c. 1744).
rhymes.source: Tommy Thumb's Pretty Song Book, London, c. 1744.
rhymes.learning_hook: counting to three, sharing, where wool comes from
rhymes.notes: Shares the 'Ah! vous dirai-je, maman' melody with Twinkle. Do not schedule the two close together.

rhymes.title: The Wheels on the Bus
rhymes.first_line: The wheels on the bus go round and round
rhymes.pd_basis: UNVERIFIED. Commonly attributed to Verna Hills, 1939 - which would still be in copyright.
rhymes.source: Attributed: Verna Hills, American Childhood magazine, 1939.
rhymes.notes: DO NOT USE. Present here deliberately as a worked example: it feels traditional and is widely treated as free, but the attribution is 1939 and the public-domain basis is unverified. The generator refuses it. Resolving this requires counsel, not a guess.
